existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Account keeps its artifact identity, but has a local hard break because `Account.partOf` was removed/replaced by `Account.parent`. The largest migration concerns are hierarchy-field transformation, R6-only billing/clinical/balance content that cannot round-trip to R4 without extensions or loss, and runtime assumptions around `description` typing and guarantor party requiredness. The main uncertainty is rationale/intent because no official diff or narrative change note was supplied.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: R4-to-R6 migration should explicitly map `partOf` to `parent`, update generated models for the changed and added fields, and review validation of Account hierarchy data. R6-to-R4 conversion needs policy decisions for optional R6-only content: drop it, carry it in extensions, map to related resources such as Encounter/Condition/Procedure/Coverage/Claim where appropriate, or reject records requiring lossless round-trip. Business logic should also be tested for guarantors without `party` and for Account subjects that intentionally differ from clinical-resource patients.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes because the local R4 and R6 snapshots/differentials were compared directly and the package indexes confirm the same canonical Account artifact. Confidence is medium for semantic intent and terminology completeness because rendered narrative, official diffs, Jira/change notes, and live terminology expansions were not available.

rationaleMd:

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 30/100, producing migration shape `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, major migration `No`, and compatibility posture `preserve-compatibility-per-change`.

2 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Treat this as a mostly stable resource. Individual hard breaks, renames, required bindings, or behavior changes should stand or fall on their own rationale and available less-breaking alternatives.

topFindings.title: Account hierarchy element changed from partOf to parent
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Account instance with `partOf` uses an element not present in the R6 Account definition; generated APIs, FHIRPath, indexes, and mappers also need the `parent` name.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Account.description type changed from string to markdown
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated model types and renderer assumptions can change from string to markdown, but this is not a clear old-valid/new-invalid instance break for ordinary string values.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds Account billing status, currency, balance, and calculation timestamp
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: strict R4 Account has no base representation for populated R6 billing status, currency, balances, or calculated-at timestamp; dropping them can change financial behavior.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds clinical billing context on Account that R4 cannot carry natively
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: populated R6 `covers`, `diagnosis`, or `procedure` content has no native R4 Account slot and will be rejected by strict R4 parsers unless transformed or carried in extensions.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Guarantor party is no longer required and guarantor can point to an Account
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 guarantor entries can omit `party` or use R6-only account/limit/rank/responsibility fields that R4 Account cannot represent natively; R6 consumers also need null-handling for a formerly required child.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Account.subject guidance now allows billing-demographic Patient divergence from clinical Patient
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the guidance changes identity expectations for some workflows, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid instance pattern and no new R6-only field on `subject`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
